title: Telemetry Anchors and Budgeted Warmup Orchestrator
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Context: Long-tail coldstart costs remain a measurable fraction of unit economics for some tenants. We need a low-risk automation that (1) anchors telemetry signals to stable prefill heuristics so operators can understand warmup tradeoffs and (2) runs a budgeted warmup orchestrator that applies tenant-level warmup credit without violating latency SLOs. Motivation: teams keep toggling aggressive prefill settings during spikes; without clear telemetry anchors it's hard to attribute cost regressions to warmup vs batch/cache settings. This PR introduces a lightweight telemetry 'anchor' layer that correlates prefill/warmup decisions with cost telemetry and a budgeted warmup orchestrator that enforces soft budget envelopes across prefills.

Summary of changes: Implemented an Anchoring layer in internal/telemetry that records canonical warmup decisions and ties them to unit-econ tags; added a BudgetedWarmupCoordinator in pkg/prefill that tracks per-tenant warmup credit, applies decay, and makes soft permit/deny decisions; added a CLI flag and small console alert to expose over-budget tenants; created unit and integration tests and a bench harness to validate behaviour under synthetic spikes. This is intentionally conservative: the orchestrator emits metrics and decisions but defaults to permissive mode for 2 weeks post-rollout.

Why this is different from existing prefill work: instead of only recommending prefill defaults, this PR creates an operational anchor (telemetry + decision traces) so that downstream analysis and autoscalers have a stable signal to attribute cost changes. The warmup coordinator enforces a budget guardrail rather than a hard cap and can be toggled per-tenant via feature flags.

Files changed (high-level): added anchor metrics and decision traces to internal/telemetry; new coordinator and policy files under pkg/prefill; added small CLI integration in cmd/prefillctl; helm value toggles under deploy/helm; docs and runbook for SRE and CS.

Testing & CI: unit tests added for anchor encoding, coordinator budgeting, and a synthetic spike integration test using scripts/bench/warmup_sim.py. CI passed with flaky prefill e2e rerun fixed by adding a 100ms wait in the test harness. Bench numbers: controlled run showed 12% reduction in coldstart token waste on a synthetic burst (with permissive mode enabled) and observability gains for attribution. Metrics emitted: prefill_anchor.decisions, prefill_anchor.unit_econ_tag, warmup_coordinator.credit_usage, warmup_coordinator.overbudget_events.

Rollout plan: dark-launch telemetry anchors in staging for 48 hours -> enable permissive orchestrator in production (no hard blocks) for tenants on alpha list -> after 2 weeks, enable alerting and console badge for overbudget tenants -> after metrics stability check, flip orchestrator to soft-enforce mode for a subset of tenants, then gradual rollout.

Runbook notes: console alert prefills/warmup_overbudget -> run prefill audit tool (docs/telemetry/anchors.md) -> consult budget trace for decision rationale. Included a short playbook for support and SRE that maps Linear ENG-2413 and ENG-2470 to observed symptoms.

Review conversation (summary embedded):
- Miguel Rivera (reviewer): "Can the coordinator be bypassed for Dedicated tenants with high priority? Also please ensure the prometheus labels include region and tenant_tier." Author reply: "Yes — added tenant bypass list and ensured region/tenant_tier labels on all anchor metrics (internal/telemetry/anchor_metrics.go)."
- Lena Cho (reviewer): "Tests look good but the integration bench was flaky locally; can we add defensive waits or retries?" Author reply: "Added a 100ms wait in the bench harness and retried CI flaky job; left a TODO to replace waits with a robust sync in follow-up PR (ENG-2470)."
- Samir Patel (approver): "Approach looks safe; prefer permissive rollout. Approving after CI green."
- Final note from author: "Squash-merged after two approvals and CI pass; dark-launch toggles documented in deploy/helm/values.prefill.yaml."

release_notes: Introduces telemetry anchors for prefill decisions and a budgeted warmup orchestrator that provides soft budget guardrails. Dark-launch by default; enables better attribution of warmup costs and allows controlled enforcement via per-tenant feature flags.
notes_for_sre: Default is permissive. To enable hard enforcement set feature flag prefill.warmup_enforce=true in helm values for selected tenants. Use console alert prefills/warmup_overbudget to triage. See docs/telemetry/anchors.md for anchor decoding and runbook.
